newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves, coupon pass possible.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves, coupon pass possible.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to inject reserves into the banking system via a round of system -- overnight or three-day -- repurchase agreements on Monday, analysts said.
They added that the Fed might also add permanent reserves to the system through a coupon pass operation.
The Fed faces an average daily add need of about $11 billion in the second half of the current maintenance period, ending Wednesday.
The 14-day fixed RP's done Thursday remain on the books, but only $6.7 billion are outstanding, analysts said.

Debate over whether the Fed will execute overnight system RPs or three day RPs centers on whether the Fed will deviate from its recent pattern of doing overnight system RPs almost every day in the current period -- with the exception of the 14-day RPs last week.
Should the Fed wish to take care of the rest of the period today, then the Fed will do three-day system RPs; if not, three more days of overnight system RPs are in the cards, analysts said.

Meanwhile, as strong demand for currency this time of year drains reserves, the Fed is expected to continue adding permanent reserves to the system by buying coupons, perhaps as early as today, some said.
Another one or two rounds of a coupon pass are likely through early April, with analysts forecasting them totaling about $5.0 billion.

"While the large size of the estimated add need argues for another round of coupon purchases, the Fed may decide to alternate its purchases and buy bills instead," noted Kathy Bostjancic, money market analyst at UBS Securities LLC.
